item.title: Dispatched at -38°C: Surviving Sub-Zero Lock Freeze-Ups on Western Manitoba Farmlands
item.description: When the thermometer dips below -35°C on the open prairie between Brandon and the Saskatchewan border, physics changes the rules of locksmithing. Metal contracts. Moisture from a brief November thaw freezes into crystalline ice dams inside the pin chambers of mortise cylinders. And when a cattle rancher in Miniota or an ag equipment operator outside Virden needs entry to a heated workshop containing vital tractors, you don’t have the luxury of waiting for spring.
